summary: Egypt's Ministry of Interior issues tourist eVisas through visa2egypt.gov.eg (30 USD single entry, 65 USD multiple entry) to the nationalities listed on the portal. The UK and Canadian governments say their citizens can also buy a visa on arrival, paid in US dollars, and the UK says visitors who fly into Sharm El-Sheikh and stay under 15 days at the resorts of Sharm El Sheikh, Dahab, Nuweiba or Taba get a free entry stamp instead.

notes: The UK government's travel advice says you must not import, use or produce drones in Egypt without prior permission from the Egyptian Ministry of Defence; doing so without permission can bring a prison sentence of up to 7 years or a fine of 5,000 to 50,000 Egyptian pounds.
Canada's travel advice says it is prohibited to export any antiquity or any item older than 100 years without a licence.

The UK government's travel advice says officials are likely to confiscate satellite phones or radio communications equipment unless you have prior clearance from the Ministry of Telecommunications, and that high-value electronic devices and recording equipment should be declared on arrival.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says major credit cards are accepted in larger stores and for larger purchases, but many merchants accept only cash or charge a fee for card payment. It adds that US dollars are preferred, particularly at tourist sites, and that some travel agents and tour operators ask for payment in US cash only.

safety.text: The UK advises against all travel to North Sinai and to within 20 km of the Libyan border, and against all but essential travel to most of the Western Desert, northern South Sinai beyond the St Catherine–Nuweiba road, Ismailiyah east of the Suez Canal and the Hala'ib Triangle.

tips.text: Apply for the Egyptian eVisa at the official portal visa2egypt.gov.eg. The UK government's travel advice says you do not need to buy a visa from an agent at the airport: agents often charge more than the 30 US dollar fee, and harassment by an agent can be reported to the tourist police in the terminal.

The UK government's travel advice says drones may not be imported or used in Egypt without prior permission from the Ministry of Defence, with penalties of up to 7 years in prison or a fine of 5,000 to 50,000 Egyptian pounds.

The UK government's travel advice says that if you arrive by air at Sharm El-Sheikh and stay less than 15 days at the resorts of Sharm El Sheikh, Dahab, Nuweiba or Taba, you get a free entry permission stamp and need no visa. To travel outside those resorts or stay longer than 15 days you need a visa, available at Sharm El-Sheikh Airport or online.

It is illegal to take photos of, or near, military property in Egypt, including the Suez Canal, according to the UK government's travel advice. Canada's travel advice adds that photographing bridges, canals, government, police and embassy buildings and vehicles, and military personnel is prohibited.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Egypt?
faq.answer: Yes. The United States is on the e-Visa portal's list of eligible nationalities: apply at visa2egypt.gov.eg (30 USD single entry, 65 USD multiple entry). The Egyptian Consulate in Washington advises getting the visa in advance, and says that from 1 September 2026 visas on arrival at Egyptian airports are issued as an electronic QR code.

faq.question: Is Egypt's visa on arrival better than the eVisa?
faq.answer: The eVisa costs 30 USD (single entry) or 65 USD (multiple entry), paid online by card at visa2egypt.gov.eg. The UK government's travel advice says getting an e-visa in advance can help prevent delays, that tourist e-visas are valid for up to 3 months and visas on arrival for up to 30 days, and that a physical visa on arrival costs 30 USD cash at approved airports, while Cairo International Airport also sells a digital one by card for 36 USD, including a 6 USD digital service fee.

faq.question: What is the free Sinai entry stamp?
faq.answer: The UK government's travel advice says that if you arrive by air at Sharm El-Sheikh and stay less than 15 days at the resorts of Sharm El Sheikh, Dahab, Nuweiba or Taba, you get a free entry permission stamp on arrival and need no visa. It does not cover travel outside those resorts or a stay longer than 15 days — for that you need a visa, available at Sharm El-Sheikh Airport or online.

faq.question: How long must my passport be valid to enter Egypt?
faq.answer: At least 6 months from your date of arrival.

faq.question: Do I need vaccinations for Egypt?
faq.answer: WHO's country list says a yellow fever certificate (ICVP) is required of travellers aged 9 months or over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, or after more than 12 hours in transit at an airport in one. It also records that Egypt requires proof of polio vaccination from travellers arriving from certain countries.
